claim.text:
All registers and channels in this page are finite-dimensional, and all entropies use natural logarithms. The operational quantum and private capacities have regularized information formulas for a general memoryless channel. The regularization is essential to the statement: no general single-letter additivity claim is made. Entanglement assistance has an additive mutual-information formula. Degradable channels admit a single-letter quantum and private formula, and the flagged erasure channel provides an exact family across both degradable and antidegradable regimes.

A channel dilation keeps the receiver's output and the environment's output side by side. The two partial traces define the channel and its complement, respectively; the formulas are given by the maps, not by the diagram.

~~~tikzcd
A \arrow[r,"V"] & B\otimes E \arrow[dl,"\\operatorname{Tr}_E"'] \arrow[dr,"\\operatorname{Tr}_B"] & \\
B & & E
~~~

For a purification on a reference register $R$ and channel input $A$, coherent information is $I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)=S(B)-S(BR)$. A Stinespring dilation gives $S(BR)=S(E)$, so the same quantity is the receiver entropy minus the environment entropy. Private information compares the Holevo information available at the receiver and environment. The capacity definitions specify their respective coding tasks and error criteria.

The entanglement-assisted one-use information is $S(\rho)+I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)=I(R;B)$, maximized over input states. Its additivity follows by applying data processing to the two local complementary channels and using nonnegative mutual information. For a degradable channel, the environment is obtained from the receiver by a channel; this makes coherent information concave and subadditive across tensor factors. The flagged erasure channel has complementary erasure probability $1-\epsilon$: for $\epsilon\le1/2$ it is degradable, for $\epsilon\ge1/2$ it is antidegradable, and at $\epsilon=1/2$ the two channels are identical up to the flag convention.

The companion examples specialize the noiseless qubit entanglement-assisted endpoint and the qudit erasure-capacity curve. The supplied Schumacher compression and HSW page provides finite-dimensional coding context; the Knill–Laflamme page fixes the separate error-correction setting; the Bell-state page supplies the dense-coding protocol used in the noiseless example.

The operational coding proofs are supplied by finite-block entropy continuity, exponential spectral-projector estimates, exact flat spectral-type reduction, finite unitary averaging and recovery, cq wiretap packing/covering with unnormalized Holevo leakage control, and flat Weyl entanglement-assisted codes. Finite ordered selections retain the stated no-choice convention. The converse arguments apply to the respective isometric quantum encoders, strong-secrecy mixed-state private codes, and arbitrary finite shared-state entanglement-assisted encoders.

export.text:
This page proves two finite-dimensional asymptotic coding theorems. For the IID source $\rho^{\otimes n}$, the Schumacher rate is $S(\rho)$ nats, measured using squared entanglement fidelity of a channel that factors through the code space. For a fixed finite-input memoryless cq channel $x\mapsto\rho_x$, the HSW capacity is the maximum ensemble Holevo information in nats/use, with deterministic codewords, collective output POVMs, and vanishing average block error. Bits are obtained by dividing the displayed nats rates by $\ln2$; no infinite-dimensional or general quantum-input single-letter claim is made.

The source-code diagram records the untouched reference register and the two channels in the code definition. The cq diagram records the encoder word, memoryless output state, and decoder measurement. These are type-level diagrams only; the statements and proofs below use the explicit channel, state, and POVM formulas.

~~~tikzcd
R\otimes A^{\otimes n} \arrow[r,"\operatorname{id}_R\otimes\mathcal E_n"] &
R\otimes C_n \arrow[r,"\operatorname{id}_R\otimes\mathcal D_n"] &
R\otimes\widehat A^{\otimes n}
~~~

~~~tikzcd
[M] \arrow[r,"m\mapsto x^n(m)"] &
\mathcal X^n \arrow[r,"x^n\mapsto\bigotimes_i\rho_{x_i}"] &
\mathcal D(H_B^{\otimes n}) \arrow[r,"\{\Lambda_m\}"] &
[M]
~~~

export.text:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root convention that its inner product is linear in the first argument, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$ ([[def-qc-density-operator]]). If $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$ are its eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, define its **von Neumann entropy** by

$$S(\rho):=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho):=-\sum_{j:\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j\ln\lambda_j.$$

The trace is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]), and the spectral definition makes the expression independent of the eigenbasis. The term for a zero eigenvalue is defined to be $0\ln0:=0$. The default unit is nats, using the natural logarithm ([[def-natural-logarithm]]); the entropy in bits is $S_2(\rho):=S(\rho)/\ln2$.

edges.actual_use: For a finite state mixture, entropy excess equals averaged finite QRE; a finite purification label marginal and its diagonal give the upper bound H(p).
consumer_fact_or_definition_quotes: [F1] [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]]: Finite-dimensional von Neumann entropy.
consumer_proof_or_symbol_use_quotes: 1.1 Omit zero weights. Positivity of $\bar\rho-p_i\rho_i$ implies $\ker\bar\rho\subseteq\ker\rho_i$ (take its quadratic form on a kernel vector), so every relative entropy below is finite. Expanding the spectral cross traces gives $$S(\bar\rho)-\sum_i p_iS(\rho_i)=\sum_i p_iD(\rho_i\Vert\bar\rho)\ge0$$ by the finite-state QRE nonnegativity supplier. [F1, F2, F3, F4, given, algebra, construct]

2.1 For the upper bound, diagonalize each $\rho_i=\sum_j\lambda_{ij}|v_{ij}\rangle\langle v_{ij}|$, omitting zero eigenvalues, and purify the mixture as $|v\rangle=\sum_{ij}\sqrt{p_i\lambda_{ij}}|v_{ij}\rangle\otimes|i,j\rangle$. Its label marginal $G$ has diagonal $q_{ij}=p_i\lambda_{ij}$ and has the same nonzero eigenvalues as $\bar\rho$ by Schmidt decomposition. [F1, F2, F3, F4, given, algebra, construct, step 1.1]

3.1 For $\Delta=\operatorname{diag}(q)$, positivity gives $\operatorname{supp}G\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\Delta$; hence $$0\le D(G\Vert\Delta)=H(q)-S(G)=H(p)+\sum_i p_iS(\rho_i)-S(\bar\rho).$$ This proves both bounds, including singleton/zero-weight cases. [F1, F2, F3, F4, given, algebra, construct, step 2.1] ∎

Natural logarithms/nats and omission of zero eigenvalues agree; bits or qubits are obtained by division by ln2.

claim.text:
For every fixed finite ensemble $p_x,\rho_x$ and fixed $\eta>0$, there are constants $C,c>0$ (depending on this ensemble and $\eta$, not $n$) and projectors $P_n,Q_{x^n}$ such that, writing $\bar\rho=\sum p_x\rho_x$ and $s=\sum p_xS(\rho_x)$,
$$\operatorname{rank}P_n\le e^{n(S(\bar\rho)+\eta)},\quad P_n\bar\rho^{\otimes n}P_n\preceq e^{-n(S(\bar\rho)-\eta)}P_n,$$
$$\operatorname{rank}Q_{x^n}\le e^{n(s+\eta)},\quad Q_{x^n}\rho_{x^n}Q_{x^n}\preceq e^{-n(s-\eta)}Q_{x^n},$$
and
$$\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{X^n}(I-P_n))\le Ce^{-cn},\qquad\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{X^n}(I-Q_{X^n}))\le Ce^{-cn}.$$
The second pair of algebraic bounds holds for every word, including words with zero sampling probability; no per-word high-acceptance assertion is required.

consumer_proof_or_symbol_use_quotes: 1.1 For $P_n$, retain product eigenvectors of $\bar\rho^{\otimes n}$ whose positive eigenvalue has negative logarithm in $n[S(\bar\rho)-\eta,S(\bar\rho)+\eta]$. For $Q_{x^n}$, use product eigenvectors of $\rho_{x^n}=\bigotimes_i\rho_{x_i}$ whose eigenvalue has negative logarithm in $n[s-\eta,s+\eta]$. The upper eigenvalue bounds are immediate. The lower retained eigenvalue and trace at most one imply each rank bound. Under the joint law $\Pr(X=x,J=j)=p_x\lambda_{xj}$, with zero-probability eigenvalues omitted, the random variable $Z=-\ln\lambda_{XJ}$ has finite support and mean $s$. Its IID sum controls the second failure probability exactly. The first failure is the same argument for the spectral law of $\bar\rho$; averaging inputs gives $\bar\rho^{\otimes n}$. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, given, algebra, construct]

2.1 For completeness, a finite supported centered variable $Y$ with $|Y|\le b$ obeys $\mathbb E e^{uY}\le1+u^2b^2e^{|u|b}/2$, by the Taylor remainder and $\mathbb EY=0$. For small fixed $u>0$, $\ln\mathbb E e^{uY}<u\eta/2$. Markov's inequality and independence then bound $\Pr(\sum Y_i\ge n\eta)\le e^{-nu\eta/2}$; apply the same argument to $-Y$ and add. A constant spectral variable has zero failure probability and needs no division by a range. All logarithms are evaluated only on positive-probability eigenvalues. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, step 1.1, given, algebra, construct] ∎

export.text:
Let $X$ be a finite nonempty classical label set, represented by a register $H_X$ with computational orthonormal basis $(\xi_x)_{x\in X}$ ([[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]]). For each $x$, write $\Pi_xz:=\langle z,\xi_x\rangle\xi_x$, the rank-one orthogonal projection using the root linear-first convention, as in [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Let $H_B$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. A finite **classical-quantum state** is

$$\rho_{XB}:=\sum_{x\in X}p_x\Pi_x\otimes\rho_x,$$

where $p_x\ge0$, $\sum_xp_x=1$, and each $\rho_x$ is a density operator on $H_B$. It is a density operator by [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Its quantum marginal is $\bar\rho_B:=\sum_xp_x\rho_x=\operatorname{Tr}_X\rho_{XB}$ by the second-factor partial-trace formula in [[def-qc-partial-trace]], and it is a density operator by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. The **Holevo information** of this ensemble is

$$\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\}_{x\in X}):=S(\bar\rho_B)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x),$$

$$\rho_{XB}:=\sum_{x\in X}p_x\Pi_x\otimes\rho_x,$$

where $p_x\ge0$, $\sum_xp_x=1$, and each $\rho_x$ is a density operator on $H_B$. It is a density operator by [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. $$\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\}_{x\in X}):=S(\bar\rho_B)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x),$$

claim.text:
Let $A$ and $B$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $\mathcal N:\mathcal L(A)\to\mathcal L(B)$ be a quantum channel as in [[def-qc-quantum-channel]]. Choose a finite-dimensional environment $E$ and a linear isometry $V:A\to B\otimes E$ such that

$$\mathcal N(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_E(VXV^*)$$

for every $X\in\mathcal L(A)$; such a dilation exists by [[thm-qc-finite-stinespring-dilation]]. The channel

$$\mathcal N^c(X):=\operatorname{Tr}_B(VXV^*)\in\mathcal L(E)$$

is the **complementary channel associated with this chosen dilation**. The partial trace $\operatorname{Tr}_B$ contracts the first factor of the ordered product $B\otimes E$ ([[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]).

It is a quantum channel: reorder $B\otimes E$ to $E\otimes B$ by the finite wire-permutation unitary ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]); the reordered $V$ is still an isometry, so tracing its second factor $B$ gives a channel by [[thm-qc-isometry-partial-trace-is-channel]].

For a density operator $\rho$ on $A$, choose a finite purification $|\psi\rangle\in A\otimes R$ with $\operatorname{Tr}_R|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|=\rho$ ([[def-qc-ensemble-and-purification]]), and define $\omega_{BR}:=(\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|)$. Its **coherent information** from $A$ to $B$ is

$$I_c(\rho,\mathcal N):=S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\omega_{BR}),$$

where $S$ is finite-dimensional von Neumann entropy in nats ([[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]]). The value does not depend on the chosen purification: after padding reference spaces, any two purifications differ by a unitary on $R$ ([[thm-qc-purification-existence-and-unitary-equivalence]]); applying $\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R$ preserves that unitary relation. A unitary maps an orthonormal eigenbasis to an orthonormal eigenbasis with the same eigenvalues, so entropy is unchanged ([[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]). Padding adds only zero eigenvalues, which do not contribute.

export.text:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root convention that its inner product is linear in the first argument, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$ ([[def-qc-density-operator]]). If $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$ are its eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, define its **von Neumann entropy** by

$$S(\rho):=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho):=-\sum_{j:\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j\ln\lambda_j.$$

The trace is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]), and the spectral definition makes the expression independent of the eigenbasis. The term for a zero eigenvalue is defined to be $0\ln0:=0$. The default unit is nats, using the natural logarithm ([[def-natural-logarithm]]); the entropy in bits is $S_2(\rho):=S(\rho)/\ln2$.

claim.text:
Let $A,B,A',B'$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, let $\rho_{AB}$ be a density operator on $A\otimes B$, and let $\Phi:A\to A'$ and $\Psi:B\to B'$ be quantum channels. Then

$$I(A':B')_{(\Phi\otimes\Psi)(\rho)}\le I(A:B)_\rho,$$

where quantum mutual information is $I(X:Y)_\omega=S(\omega_X)+S(\omega_Y)-S(\omega_{XY})$ as in [[def-it-finite-quantum-information-measures]].

export.text:
For a finite bipartite state $\rho_{AB}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B$, write $\rho_A=\operatorname{Tr}_B\rho_{AB}$ and $\rho_B=\operatorname{Tr}_A\rho_{AB}$, using the partial traces in [[def-qc-partial-trace]] and [[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]. They are states by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. Define

$$S(A)_\rho:=S(\rho_A),\qquad S(A\mid B)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AB})-S(\rho_B),\qquad I(A:B)_\rho:=S(\rho_A)+S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{AB}).$$

For a finite tripartite state $\rho_{ABC}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C$, set $\rho_{AB}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_C}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying the factors as $(H_A\otimes H_B)\otimes H_C$, and $\rho_{BC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_A}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying them as $H_A\otimes(H_B\otimes H_C)$. Let $P:H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C\to H_A\otimes H_C\otimes H_B$ be the wire permutation taking factor order $A,B,C$ to $A,C,B$ ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]) and set $\rho_{AC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}(P\rho_{ABC}P^*)$, tracing out the last factor. Because $P$ is unitary, $P\rho_{ABC}P^*$ is a state: unitary conjugation preserves non-negativity by the adjoint identity ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]) and preserves trace by cyclicity ([[thm-trace-of-ab-equals-trace-of-ba]]). Finally set $\rho_C:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}\rho_{BC}$. All these marginals are density operators by applying [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]] after grouping factors. Define

$$I(A:B\mid C)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AC})+S(\rho_{BC})-S(\rho_C)-S(\rho_{ABC}).$$

These are finite-dimensional definitions only; no non-negativity of conditional entropy or conditional mutual information is part of the notation.

3.1 Repeat step 1.1–2.1 with $\Psi$ acting on the second register, now taking the first register to be $A'$. $$I(A:B\mid C)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AC})+S(\rho_{BC})-S(\rho_C)-S(\rho_{ABC}).$$

export.text:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root convention that its inner product is linear in the first argument, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$ ([[def-qc-density-operator]]). If $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$ are its eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, define its **von Neumann entropy** by

$$S(\rho):=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho):=-\sum_{j:\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j\ln\lambda_j.$$

The trace is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]), and the spectral definition makes the expression independent of the eigenbasis. The term for a zero eigenvalue is defined to be $0\ln0:=0$. The default unit is nats, using the natural logarithm ([[def-natural-logarithm]]); the entropy in bits is $S_2(\rho):=S(\rho)/\ln2$.

export.text:
Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $A,B:H\to H$ be non-negative operators. For such an operator $A$, set $\operatorname{supp}(A):=(\ker A)^\perp$, where $\ker A$ is the kernel of a linear map ([[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]); this extends the density-operator support convention in [[def-qc-density-operator]]. If $\operatorname{supp}(A)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(B)$, define

$$D(A\|B):=\operatorname{tr}(A\ln A)-\operatorname{tr}(A\ln B).$$

Here $\ln A$ is defined spectrally on the positive eigenspaces of $A$ with $0\ln0:=0$, and $\ln B$ in the cross term is restricted to $\operatorname{supp}(B)$; the support condition ensures that $A$ vanishes on $\ker B$, so the omitted kernel contributes zero. If $\operatorname{supp}(A)\nsubseteq\operatorname{supp}(B)$, set $D(A\|B):=+\infty$. In particular, $D(0\|B)=0$. For density operators this is the finite-dimensional **quantum relative entropy**. The logarithms are natural, so the value is in nats; the base-two value is $D_2(A\|B):=D(A\|B)/\ln2$.

Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $A,B:H\to H$ be non-negative operators. For such an operator $A$, set $\operatorname{supp}(A):=(\ker A)^\perp$, where $\ker A$ is the kernel of a linear map ([[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]); this extends the density-operator support convention in [[def-qc-density-operator]]. If $\operatorname{supp}(A)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(B)$, define

$$D(A\|B):=\operatorname{tr}(A\ln A)-\operatorname{tr}(A\ln B).$$

Here $\ln A$ is defined spectrally on the positive eigenspaces of $A$ with $0\ln0:=0$, and $\ln B$ in the cross term is restricted to $\operatorname{supp}(B)$; the support condition ensures that $A$ vanishes on $\ker B$, so the omitted kernel contributes zero. If $\operatorname{supp}(A)\nsubseteq\operatorname{supp}(B)$, set $D(A\|B):=+\infty$. In particular, $D(0\|B)=0$. For density operators this is the finite-dimensional **quantum relative entropy**. The logarithms are natural, so the value is in nats; the base-two value is $D_2(A\|B):=D(A\|B)/\ln2$.

Let $\rho$ be a density operator on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$, let $0\preceq\Lambda\preceq I_H$, and suppose $\operatorname{tr}(\Lambda\rho)\ge1-u$ for some $u\in[0,1]$. Then

$$\left\|\rho-\sqrt{\Lambda}\rho\sqrt{\Lambda}\right\|_1\le2\sqrt{u}.$$

consumer_proof_or_symbol_use_quotes: 1.1 Set $s_B=S(\mathcal N(\tau))$, $s_E=S(\mathcal N^c(\tau))$. Choose $\eta>0$ with $R<s_B-s_E-2\eta$. On $n$ uses, let $|v_n\rangle=(I\otimes V^{\otimes n})|\Phi_{d^n}\rangle$ in factor order $A'B^nE^n$. Let $P_n,Q_n$ be the spectral projectors for the IID receiver and environment states from [[lem-it-exponential-cq-spectral-projectors]], and let $\epsilon_n\le Ce^{-cn}$ bound the sum of their failure probabilities. The commuting joint projection has acceptance at least $1-\epsilon_n$. For $$|\widehat v_n\rangle=(I_{A'}\otimes P_n\otimes Q_n)|v_n\rangle,$$ the rank-two pure-vector calculation used in gentle measurement gives $$\bigl\||v_n\rangle\langle v_n|-|\widehat v_n\rangle\langle\widehat v_n|\bigr\|_1\le2\sqrt{\epsilon_n}.$$ This follows also by applying the gentle-measurement lemma to the pure state and the joint projection. Let $\omega=\operatorname{Tr}_{B^n}|\widehat v_n\rangle\langle\widehat v_n|$. Its environment rank is at most $e^{n(s_E+\eta)}$. Since the projected vector is pure, $$\operatorname{tr}(\omega^2)=\operatorname{tr}(\omega_{B^n}^2).$$ Moreover $$0\preceq\omega_{B^n}\preceq P_n\mathcal N(\tau)^{\otimes n}P_n\preceq e^{-n(s_B-\eta)}P_n.$$ To verify the first inequality, take the partial trace after $Q_n$; the complementary environment projection produces another positive summand of the original receiver marginal. Hence $\operatorname{tr}(\omega^2)\le e^{-n(s_B-\eta)}$, because its trace is at most one. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, F8, F9, F10, given, algebra, construct]

2.1 Take $K_n=\lfloor e^{nR}\rfloor$. It is at most $d^n$: subadditivity on the pure Stinespring output implies $s_B\le\ln d+s_E$. If $I_c>0$ then $d\ge2$. For an isometry $W:\mathbb C^{K_n}\to(\mathbb C^d)^{\otimes n}$, let $\rho^W_{RE^n}$ be the environment/reference state produced by encoding half of $|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle$. Coefficient matrices give exactly the normalized-compression expression for the unprojected marginal. Use the finite ensemble above with tolerance $e^{-n}$. Apply its compression estimate to $\omega$, and its averaged trace-contraction estimate to the difference between projected and unprojected marginals. Their environment marginals differ by at most $2\sqrt{\epsilon_n}$. The triangle inequality therefore yields $$\mathbb E\left\|\rho^W_{RE^n}-\frac{I_R}{K_n}\otimes\mathcal N^c(\tau)^{\otimes n}\right\|_1 \le6\sqrt{\epsilon_n}+2e^{-n}+\sqrt{2e^{-n(s_B-s_E-R-2\eta)}}\longrightarrow0.$$ Order the finite generator list and its length-$L$ words. For each $n$, take the first word whose displayed norm is at most twice its expectation; if that expectation is zero, take the first zero-norm word. A qualifying word exists by finite averaging. This specifies the entire encoder sequence without countable choices. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, F8, F9, F10, step 1.1, given, algebra, construct]

3.1 The product target is purified by $|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle_{RM}\otimes|e_n\rangle_{E^nF}$, with a sufficiently large finite $F$. The encoded Stinespring output is another purification on reference/environment versus receiver. Root-fidelity purification characterization, after adding a pure finite ancilla to the receiver if needed, supplies an isometry on the receiver's purifying space whose overlap with that target is the root fidelity of the two marginals. The fixed-purification form follows from the purification/unitary-equivalence theorem. Fuchs–van de Graaf makes this root fidelity at least one minus half the displayed norm. Trace out the extra decoder factor $F$: the resulting CPTP decoder has squared entanglement fidelity at least the square of that overlap and hence tending to one. The encoder is exactly the isometry $W$; no generating-code/transmitting-code equivalence is assumed. Fix ordered bases throughout. In the purification characterization use the polar/SVD attaining map, extending every kernel partial isometry by the ordered basis completion; in repeated eigenspaces, project the ordered coordinate vectors and Gram–Schmidt in that order. This specifies a decoder at each block length by one formula, rather than choosing a sequence of unrelated attaining maps. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, F8, F9, F10, step 2.1, given, algebra, construct] ∎

Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional channel, let $V:A\to B\otimes E$ be a finite Stinespring isometry, let $\mathcal N^c(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_B(VXV^*)$, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $A$. Then

$$I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)=S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\mathcal N^c(\rho)).$$

export.text:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root convention that its inner product is linear in the first argument, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$ ([[def-qc-density-operator]]). If $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$ are its eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, define its **von Neumann entropy** by

$$S(\rho):=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho):=-\sum_{j:\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j\ln\lambda_j.$$

The trace is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]), and the spectral definition makes the expression independent of the eigenbasis. The term for a zero eigenvalue is defined to be $0\ln0:=0$. The default unit is nats, using the natural logarithm ([[def-natural-logarithm]]); the entropy in bits is $S_2(\rho):=S(\rho)/\ln2$.

As the left side of the formula is independent of both the purification and the chosen complement, the right side has the same value for every finite dilation. [F1, F3, F5, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

prior_rows.excerpt:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root convention that its inner product is linear in the first argument, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$ ([[def-qc-density-operator]]). If $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$ are its eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, define its **von Neumann entropy** by

$$S(\rho):=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho):=-\sum_{j:\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j\ln\lambda_j.$$

The trace is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]), and the spectral definition makes the expression independent of the eigenbasis. The term for a zero eigenvalue is defined to be $0\ln0:=0$. The default unit is nats, using the natural logarithm ([[def-natural-logarithm]]); the entropy in bits is $S_2(\rho):=S(\rho)/\ln2$.

claim.text:
Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional quantum channel, fix its complementary channel $\mathcal N^c:A\to E$, and let $\mathcal E=\{p_x,\rho_x\}_{x\in\mathcal X}$ be a finite ensemble of density operators on $A$. Set $\bar\rho:=\sum_xp_x\rho_x$. Its **private information** is

$$I_p(\mathcal E,\mathcal N):=\chi(\{p_x,\mathcal N(\rho_x)\})-\chi(\{p_x,\mathcal N^c(\rho_x)\}),$$

where $\chi$ is the Holevo information from [[def-it-classical-quantum-state-and-holevo-information]]; zero-probability terms are omitted. Equivalently, it is the mutual information between the classical label and the receiver output minus that between the label and the complementary output.

export.text:
Let $X$ be a finite nonempty classical label set, represented by a register $H_X$ with computational orthonormal basis $(\xi_x)_{x\in X}$ ([[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]]). For each $x$, write $\Pi_xz:=\langle z,\xi_x\rangle\xi_x$, the rank-one orthogonal projection using the root linear-first convention, as in [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Let $H_B$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. A finite **classical-quantum state** is

$$\rho_{XB}:=\sum_{x\in X}p_x\Pi_x\otimes\rho_x,$$

where $p_x\ge0$, $\sum_xp_x=1$, and each $\rho_x$ is a density operator on $H_B$. It is a density operator by [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Its quantum marginal is $\bar\rho_B:=\sum_xp_x\rho_x=\operatorname{Tr}_X\rho_{XB}$ by the second-factor partial-trace formula in [[def-qc-partial-trace]], and it is a density operator by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. The **Holevo information** of this ensemble is

$$\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\}_{x\in X}):=S(\bar\rho_B)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x),$$

where zero-probability branches contribute nothing. This is measured in nats under [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]].

claim.text: Fix any finite input ensemble $(p_x,\rho_x)$ for a finite-dimensional channel $\mathcal N$ and a complement $\mathcal N^c$. Let $\chi_B,\chi_E$ be the Holevo informations of their output ensembles. Every $0<R<\chi_B-\chi_E$ admits uniform $M_n$-message codes with mixed input states, Bob POVMs, $n^{-1}\ln M_n\to R$, average error tending to zero, and unnormalized complementary-output Holevo leakage tending to zero. The construction has exponentially decaying average error and average trace distance to a fixed complementary product target; dimension-dependent entropy control converts the latter to strong Holevo secrecy.

export.text:
Let $\rho$ be a density operator on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$, let $0\preceq\Lambda\preceq I_H$, and suppose $\operatorname{tr}(\Lambda\rho)\ge1-u$ for some $u\in[0,1]$. Then

$$\left\|\rho-\sqrt{\Lambda}\rho\sqrt{\Lambda}\right\|_1\le2\sqrt{u}.$$

Here $\sqrt{\Lambda}$ is the unique nonnegative square root, and $\|\cdot\|_1$ is the finite-dimensional trace norm. No normalization is applied after the operation $\rho\mapsto\sqrt{\Lambda}\rho\sqrt{\Lambda}$.

edges.actual_use: Finite random mixed-input wiretap codes use square-root POVM packing, projected variance covering, exponential trace approximation and dimension-dependent entropy control to prove unnormalized Holevo strong secrecy.
consumer_fact_or_definition_quotes: [F3] [[lem-it-finite-gentle-measurement]]: Gentle measurement bound in finite dimensions.
consumer_proof_or_symbol_use_quotes: 1.1 Choose $r$with $\chi_E<r$ and $R+r<\chi_B$, and then choose $\eta>0$ so $r>\chi_E+2\eta$ and $R+r<\chi_B-2\eta$. Take $M_n=\lfloor e^{nR}\rfloor$, $L_n=\lceil e^{nr}\rceil$ and draw $M_nL_n$ independent words $X^n(m,l)$ with law $p^{\otimes n}$. For message $m$, the encoder inputs the mixed state $$\rho_{m,n}=\frac1{L_n}\sum_{l=1}^{L_n}\bigotimes_{i=1}^n\rho_{X_i(m,l)}.$$ This is a legitimate finite private randomization of the operational input state; the realized codebook is public. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, F8, given, algebra, construct]

2.1 For Bob use the global and conditional spectral projectors $P,Q_{x^n}$ from [[lem-it-exponential-cq-spectral-projectors]], for the receiver ensemble. Put $\Gamma_{m,l}=P Q_{X^n(m,l)}P$, form the square-root POVM from all $\Gamma_{m,l}$, and assign its kernel/failure outcome to one message. The finite Hayashi–Nagaoka operator inequality bounds each pair-decoding error by twice its own projector failure plus four times its interference sum. The estimate is valid without a uniform per-word projector-acceptance hypothesis: only its average is needed here. Specifically, $$\mathbb E[1-\operatorname{tr}(\Gamma_{m,l}\beta_{X^n(m,l)})]\le\varepsilon_n+2\sqrt{\varepsilon_n},$$ where $\varepsilon_n\le Ce^{-cn}$ bounds both averaged projector failures. This follows by $\operatorname{tr}(Q_xP\beta_xP)\ge\operatorname{tr}(Q_x\beta_x)-\|P\beta_xP-\beta_x\|_1$ and the gentle-measurement bound followed by Jensen. For two different independent codewords, the spectral eigenvalue and rank bounds give $$\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(\Gamma_j\beta_{X_i^n}) =\operatorname{tr}[(P\mathbb E Q_{X_j^n}P)(P\bar\beta^{\otimes n}P)] \le e^{-n(S(\bar\beta)-\eta)}e^{n(\sum_xp_xS(\beta_x)+\eta)} =e^{-n(\chi_B-2\eta)}.$$ The equality uses the support of the first factor; the inequality uses positivity of the operator-order difference, not commutation of the two factors. Thus expected pair-error is at most $$2(\varepsilon_n+2\sqrt{\varepsilon_n})+4M_nL_ne^{-n(\chi_B-2\eta)},$$ which decays exponentially. Coarsening the pair POVM to its message label cannot increase message error. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, F8, step 1.1, given, algebra, construct]

3.1 For Eve let $P,Q_{x^n}$ denote the spectral projectors for her ensemble, put $s_E=\sum_xp_xS(\epsilon_x)$, and define $$\xi_{x^n}=P Q_{x^n}\epsilon_{x^n}Q_{x^n}P,\qquad\theta=\mathbb E\xi_{X^n}.$$ These operators satisfy $0\preceq\xi_{x^n}\preceq e^{-n(s_E-\eta)}P$, $\operatorname{tr}\xi_{x^n}\le1$, and $\operatorname{rank}P\le e^{n(S(\bar\epsilon)+\eta)}$. Their average truncation error obeys $$\mathbb E\|\epsilon_{X^n}-\xi_{X^n}\|_1\le\zeta_n:=\varepsilon_n+2\sqrt{\varepsilon_n}.$$ Indeed the conditional projector commutes with its state, so its trace-norm loss equals its failure probability. Its subnormalized output $A$ satisfies $0\preceq A\preceq\epsilon_{x^n}$, and the global-projection loss is at most $2\sqrt{\operatorname{tr}[(I-P)A]}\le2\sqrt{\operatorname{tr}[(I-P)\epsilon_{x^n}]}$. The subnormalized gentle estimate follows by applying the normalized lemma to $A/\operatorname{tr}A$ and multiplying back (the zero operator is immediate). Jensen gives the stated averaged bound. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, F8, step 2.1, given, algebra, construct]

4.1 For the $L_n$ independent words of a fixed message, centered Hilbert–Schmidt variance gives $$\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}\left[\left(\frac1{L_n}\sum_l\xi_{X^n(m,l)}-\theta\right)^2\right] =\frac1{L_n}\{\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(\xi_{X^n}^2)-\operatorname{tr}(\theta^2)\} \le\frac{e^{-n(s_E-\eta)}}{L_n}.$$ All cross terms have zero expectation by independence. The difference is supported in $P$. Cauchy–Schwarz on singular values and Jensen imply $$\mathbb E\left\|\frac1{L_n}\sum_l\xi_{X^n(m,l)}-\theta\right\|_1\le\sqrt{\frac{e^{n(\chi_E+2\eta)}}{L_n}}.$$ Together with $\|\theta-\bar\epsilon^{\otimes n}\|_1\le\zeta_n$, this proves $$\mathbb E\left\|\tau_{m,n}-\bar\epsilon^{\otimes n}\right\|_1\le2\zeta_n+\sqrt{\frac{e^{n(\chi_E+2\eta)}}{L_n}},\qquad\tau_{m,n}=(\mathcal N^c)^{\otimes n}(\rho_{m,n}).$$ The right side decays exponentially and is independent of $m$. Consequently the expectation of the sum of average decoding error and average half-trace distance from this target decays exponentially. The codebook sample space is finite, so order the finite word/codebook alphabet and select its first deterministic codebook whose sum is at most twice its expectation (or zero if that expectation vanishes). This defines a sequence without countable choices. For that codebook let $a_n=M_n^{-1}\sum_m T(\tau_{m,n},\bar\epsilon^{\otimes n})$. The proved quantitative entropy estimate yields $$\ell_n\le2a_n n\ln\dim E+2g(a_n)\longrightarrow0.$$ This establishes the required unnormalized Holevo strong secrecy; a mere limit of trace distance without this dimension/error-rate estimate would not suffice. The average decoding error also tends to zero, while $n^{-1}\ln M_n\to R$. If the ensemble's private information is nonpositive it gives no positive lower bound; rate zero remains achievable with one message. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, F8, step 3.1, given, algebra, construct] ∎

The export bounds the unnormalized post-operation trace norm by 2 sqrt(u); for a subnormalized input the wiretap proof divides by its trace, applies the normalized lemma, then multiplies back, with zero case separate.

Let $S,T$ be nonnegative endomorphisms of a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$, with $S\preceq I_H$. Define $(S+T)^{-1/2}$ spectrally on $\operatorname{supp}(S+T)$ and set it to zero on $\ker(S+T)$. Then

$$I_H-(S+T)^{-1/2}S(S+T)^{-1/2}\preceq2(I_H-S)+4T.$$

claim.text: Fix any finite input ensemble $(p_x,\rho_x)$ for a finite-dimensional channel $\mathcal N$ and a complement $\mathcal N^c$. Let $\chi_B,\chi_E$ be the Holevo informations of their output ensembles. Every $0<R<\chi_B-\chi_E$ admits uniform $M_n$-message codes with mixed input states, Bob POVMs, $n^{-1}\ln M_n\to R$, average error tending to zero, and unnormalized complementary-output Holevo leakage tending to zero. The construction has exponentially decaying average error and average trace distance to a fixed complementary product target; dimension-dependent entropy control converts the latter to strong Holevo secrecy.

export.text:
Let $X$ be a finite nonempty classical label set, represented by a register $H_X$ with computational orthonormal basis $(\xi_x)_{x\in X}$ ([[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]]). For each $x$, write $\Pi_xz:=\langle z,\xi_x\rangle\xi_x$, the rank-one orthogonal projection using the root linear-first convention, as in [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Let $H_B$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. A finite **classical-quantum state** is

$$\rho_{XB}:=\sum_{x\in X}p_x\Pi_x\otimes\rho_x,$$

where $p_x\ge0$, $\sum_xp_x=1$, and each $\rho_x$ is a density operator on $H_B$. It is a density operator by [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Its quantum marginal is $\bar\rho_B:=\sum_xp_x\rho_x=\operatorname{Tr}_X\rho_{XB}$ by the second-factor partial-trace formula in [[def-qc-partial-trace]], and it is a density operator by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. The **Holevo information** of this ensemble is

$$\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\}_{x\in X}):=S(\bar\rho_B)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x),$$

where zero-probability branches contribute nothing. This is measured in nats under [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]].

consumer_proof_or_symbol_use_quotes: 1.1 Choose $r$with $\chi_E<r$ and $R+r<\chi_B$, and then choose $\eta>0$ so $r>\chi_E+2\eta$ and $R+r<\chi_B-2\eta$. Take $M_n=\lfloor e^{nR}\rfloor$, $L_n=\lceil e^{nr}\rceil$ and draw $M_nL_n$ independent words $X^n(m,l)$ with law $p^{\otimes n}$. For message $m$, the encoder inputs the mixed state $$\rho_{m,n}=\frac1{L_n}\sum_{l=1}^{L_n}\bigotimes_{i=1}^n\rho_{X_i(m,l)}.$$ This is a legitimate finite private randomization of the operational input state; the realized codebook is public. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, F8, given, algebra, construct]

2.1 For Bob use the global and conditional spectral projectors $P,Q_{x^n}$ from [[lem-it-exponential-cq-spectral-projectors]], for the receiver ensemble. Put $\Gamma_{m,l}=P Q_{X^n(m,l)}P$, form the square-root POVM from all $\Gamma_{m,l}$, and assign its kernel/failure outcome to one message. The finite Hayashi–Nagaoka operator inequality bounds each pair-decoding error by twice its own projector failure plus four times its interference sum. The estimate is valid without a uniform per-word projector-acceptance hypothesis: only its average is needed here. Specifically, $$\mathbb E[1-\operatorname{tr}(\Gamma_{m,l}\beta_{X^n(m,l)})]\le\varepsilon_n+2\sqrt{\varepsilon_n},$$ where $\varepsilon_n\le Ce^{-cn}$ bounds both averaged projector failures. This follows by $\operatorname{tr}(Q_xP\beta_xP)\ge\operatorname{tr}(Q_x\beta_x)-\|P\beta_xP-\beta_x\|_1$ and the gentle-measurement bound followed by Jensen. For two different independent codewords, the spectral eigenvalue and rank bounds give $$\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(\Gamma_j\beta_{X_i^n}) =\operatorname{tr}[(P\mathbb E Q_{X_j^n}P)(P\bar\beta^{\otimes n}P)] \le e^{-n(S(\bar\beta)-\eta)}e^{n(\sum_xp_xS(\beta_x)+\eta)} =e^{-n(\chi_B-2\eta)}.$$ The equality uses the support of the first factor; the inequality uses positivity of the operator-order difference, not commutation of the two factors. Thus expected pair-error is at most $$2(\varepsilon_n+2\sqrt{\varepsilon_n})+4M_nL_ne^{-n(\chi_B-2\eta)},$$ which decays exponentially. Coarsening the pair POVM to its message label cannot increase message error. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, F8, step 1.1, given, algebra, construct]

Their average truncation error obeys $$\mathbb E\|\epsilon_{X^n}-\xi_{X^n}\|_1\le\zeta_n:=\varepsilon_n+2\sqrt{\varepsilon_n}.$$ Indeed the conditional projector commutes with its state, so its trace-norm loss equals its failure probability. Its subnormalized output $A$ satisfies $0\preceq A\preceq\epsilon_{x^n}$, and the global-projection loss is at most $2\sqrt{\operatorname{tr}[(I-P)A]}\le2\sqrt{\operatorname{tr}[(I-P)\epsilon_{x^n}]}$. The subnormalized gentle estimate follows by applying the normalized lemma to $A/\operatorname{tr}A$ and multiplying back (the zero operator is immediate). Jensen gives the stated averaged bound. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, F8, step 2.1, given, algebra, construct]

4.1 For the $L_n$ independent words of a fixed message, centered Hilbert–Schmidt variance gives $$\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}\left[\left(\frac1{L_n}\sum_l\xi_{X^n(m,l)}-\theta\right)^2\right] =\frac1{L_n}\{\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(\xi_{X^n}^2)-\operatorname{tr}(\theta^2)\} \le\frac{e^{-n(s_E-\eta)}}{L_n}.$$ All cross terms have zero expectation by independence. The difference is supported in $P$. Cauchy–Schwarz on singular values and Jensen imply $$\mathbb E\left\|\frac1{L_n}\sum_l\xi_{X^n(m,l)}-\theta\right\|_1\le\sqrt{\frac{e^{n(\chi_E+2\eta)}}{L_n}}.$$ Together with $\|\theta-\bar\epsilon^{\otimes n}\|_1\le\zeta_n$, this proves $$\mathbb E\left\|\tau_{m,n}-\bar\epsilon^{\otimes n}\right\|_1\le2\zeta_n+\sqrt{\frac{e^{n(\chi_E+2\eta)}}{L_n}},\qquad\tau_{m,n}=(\mathcal N^c)^{\otimes n}(\rho_{m,n}).$$ The right side decays exponentially and is independent of $m$. Consequently the expectation of the sum of average decoding error and average half-trace distance from this target decays exponentially. The codebook sample space is finite, so order the finite word/codebook alphabet and select its first deterministic codebook whose sum is at most twice its expectation (or zero if that expectation vanishes). This defines a sequence without countable choices. For that codebook let $a_n=M_n^{-1}\sum_m T(\tau_{m,n},\bar\epsilon^{\otimes n})$. The average decoding error also tends to zero, while $n^{-1}\ln M_n\to R$. If the ensemble's private information is nonpositive it gives no positive lower bound; rate zero remains achievable with one message. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, F8, step 3.1, given, algebra, construct] ∎

Let $x\mapsto\rho_x$ be a finite-input, finite-output memoryless cq channel as in [[def-it-classical-quantum-memoryless-channel]]. With the average-error code convention of [[def-it-cq-channel-block-code-and-error]], its classical capacity in nats per use is
$$C_{\rm cq}=\max_{p\in\Delta(\mathcal X)}\chi_p,\qquad \chi_p:=S\!\left(\sum_xp_x\rho_x\right)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x).$$
For every $0\le R<C_{\rm cq}$ a sequence of codes with rate tending to $R$ has average error tending to zero, and every reliable sequence has limiting upper rate at most $C_{\rm cq}$. This theorem concerns a fixed finite classical input alphabet and does not assert a single-letter formula for general quantum-input channels.

consumer_proof_or_symbol_use_quotes: 1.1 Fix a $D$-dimensional subspace of the input, with embedding $J$ and flat state $\tau=JJ^*/D$. Share $|\Phi_D\rangle$ between the sender's subspace and a receiver reference $R$. On the sender half apply the $D^2$ Weyl unitaries, each uniformly likely, before the input embedding. The Weyl matrices in the fixed ordered basis are $U_{ab}|j\rangle=e^{2\pi i bj/D}|j+a\pmod D\rangle$. Direct summation over $b$ kills off-diagonal matrix units; summation over $a$ gives the maximally mixed diagonal. Consequently their average action on the sender half of $\Phi_D$ gives $I_D/D\otimes I_R/D$. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, given, algebra, construct]

2.1 Let $\sigma_{ab}$ be the joint output on $B R$ of this finite cq alphabet through $\mathcal N$. Because $(U_{ab}\otimes I)|\Phi_D\rangle=(I\otimes U_{ab}^T)|\Phi_D\rangle$ in coefficient coordinates, all $\sigma_{ab}$ are related by a unitary on $R$ and have identical entropy $S(\mathcal N^c(\tau))$ by purity of the full Stinespring output. Their average is $\mathcal N(\tau)\otimes I_R/D$. Thus the ensemble Holevo information is exactly $$\chi=\ln D+S(\mathcal N(\tau))-S(\mathcal N^c(\tau))=f_{\mathcal N}(\tau).$$ The HSW theorem applies to this fixed finite cq channel $ab\mapsto\sigma_{ab}$, with output $B R$. Each cq codeword is physically implemented by its sequence of Weyl operations on independent shared maximally entangled pairs. Its collective POVM is a permitted receiver measurement and its rate/error are exactly those of HSW. Therefore every nonnegative rate strictly below $f_{\mathcal N}(\tau)$ is entanglement-assisted achievable. Dimension $D=1$ is included: the one-letter ensemble then has Holevo information zero. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, step 1.1, given, algebra, construct] ∎

export.text:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root convention that its inner product is linear in the first argument, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$ ([[def-qc-density-operator]]). If $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$ are its eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, define its **von Neumann entropy** by

$$S(\rho):=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho):=-\sum_{j:\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j\ln\lambda_j.$$

The trace is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]), and the spectral definition makes the expression independent of the eigenbasis. The term for a zero eigenvalue is defined to be $0\ln0:=0$. The default unit is nats, using the natural logarithm ([[def-natural-logarithm]]); the entropy in bits is $S_2(\rho):=S(\rho)/\ln2$.

claim.text:
Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional channel with chosen complement $\mathcal N^c:A\to E$, and let $\mathcal E=\{p_x,\rho_x\}_{x\in\mathcal X}$ be a finite ensemble on $A$ with $\bar\rho=\sum_xp_x\rho_x$. Then

$$I_p(\mathcal E,\mathcal N)=I_c(\bar\rho,\mathcal N)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_x I_c(\rho_x,\mathcal N).$$

export.text:
Let $X$ be a finite nonempty classical label set, represented by a register $H_X$ with computational orthonormal basis $(\xi_x)_{x\in X}$ ([[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]]). For each $x$, write $\Pi_xz:=\langle z,\xi_x\rangle\xi_x$, the rank-one orthogonal projection using the root linear-first convention, as in [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Let $H_B$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. A finite **classical-quantum state** is

$$\rho_{XB}:=\sum_{x\in X}p_x\Pi_x\otimes\rho_x,$$

where $p_x\ge0$, $\sum_xp_x=1$, and each $\rho_x$ is a density operator on $H_B$. It is a density operator by [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Its quantum marginal is $\bar\rho_B:=\sum_xp_x\rho_x=\operatorname{Tr}_X\rho_{XB}$ by the second-factor partial-trace formula in [[def-qc-partial-trace]], and it is a density operator by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. The **Holevo information** of this ensemble is

$$\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\}_{x\in X}):=S(\bar\rho_B)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x),$$

where zero-probability branches contribute nothing. This is measured in nats under [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]].

consumer_proof_or_symbol_use_quotes: 2.1 Regrouping the finite sums in step 1.1 gives $[S(\bar B)-\sum_xp_xS(B_x)]-[S(\bar E)-\sum_xp_xS(E_x)]$. Each bracket is the corresponding Holevo information by [F2], so their difference is $I_p(\mathcal E,\mathcal N)$ by [F1]. Terms with $p_x=0$ are absent in both sums. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

Holevo information is S(average)-sum over positive weights p_x S(rho_x), in nats; zero-weight branches contribute nothing.

claim.text:
For a finite-dimensional channel $\mathcal N:A\to B$, define

$$f_{\mathcal N}(\rho):=S(\rho)+I_c(\rho,\mathcal N),\qquad F(\mathcal N):=\sup_{\rho\in\mathcal D(A)}f_{\mathcal N}(\rho).$$

For any two finite-dimensional channels $\mathcal N_i:A_i\to B_i$,

$$F(\mathcal N_1\otimes\mathcal N_2)=F(\mathcal N_1)+F(\mathcal N_2).$$

export.text:
For a finite bipartite state $\rho_{AB}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B$, write $\rho_A=\operatorname{Tr}_B\rho_{AB}$ and $\rho_B=\operatorname{Tr}_A\rho_{AB}$, using the partial traces in [[def-qc-partial-trace]] and [[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]. They are states by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. Define

$$S(A)_\rho:=S(\rho_A),\qquad S(A\mid B)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AB})-S(\rho_B),\qquad I(A:B)_\rho:=S(\rho_A)+S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{AB}).$$

For a finite tripartite state $\rho_{ABC}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C$, set $\rho_{AB}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_C}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying the factors as $(H_A\otimes H_B)\otimes H_C$, and $\rho_{BC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_A}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying them as $H_A\otimes(H_B\otimes H_C)$. Let $P:H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C\to H_A\otimes H_C\otimes H_B$ be the wire permutation taking factor order $A,B,C$ to $A,C,B$ ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]) and set $\rho_{AC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}(P\rho_{ABC}P^*)$, tracing out the last factor. Because $P$ is unitary, $P\rho_{ABC}P^*$ is a state: unitary conjugation preserves non-negativity by the adjoint identity ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]) and preserves trace by cyclicity ([[thm-trace-of-ab-equals-trace-of-ba]]). Finally set $\rho_C:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}\rho_{BC}$. All these marginals are density operators by applying [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]] after grouping factors. Define

$$I(A:B\mid C)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AC})+S(\rho_{BC})-S(\rho_C)-S(\rho_{ABC}).$$

These are finite-dimensional definitions only; no non-negativity of conditional entropy or conditional mutual information is part of the notation.

edges.actual_use: Expands the optimized-information tensor difference as -I(A1:A2)-I(B1:B2)+I(E1:E2); local complement data processing and nonnegative MI give subadditivity, while product inputs attain the reverse bound.
consumer_fact_or_definition_quotes: [F2] [[def-it-finite-quantum-information-measures]]: $I(X:Y)=S(X)+S(Y)-S(XY)$ for finite bipartite states.
consumer_proof_or_symbol_use_quotes: 1.1 Strong subadditivity [F4] with the middle register one-dimensional gives subadditivity $S(XY)\le S(X)+S(Y)$ for every bipartite state: tensoring with the unique one-dimensional state leaves all nontrivial spectra unchanged. Thus $I(X:Y)\ge0$ by [F2]. [F2, F4, given, algebra]

2.1 Fix an arbitrary state $\rho_{A_1A_2}$, and set $\rho_i$ to its marginals, $\omega_{B_1B_2}=(\mathcal N_1\otimes\mathcal N_2)(\rho)$, and $\eta_{E_1E_2}=(\mathcal N_1^c\otimes\mathcal N_2^c)(\rho)$ using product Stinespring dilations. Expanding each entropy by [F1] and each mutual information by [F2] yields $f_{\mathcal N_1\otimes\mathcal N_2}(\rho)-f_{\mathcal N_1}(\rho_1)-f_{\mathcal N_2}(\rho_2)=-I(A_1:A_2)_\rho-I(B_1:B_2)_\omega+I(E_1:E_2)_\eta$. By [F3] applied to the local complementary channels, $I(E_1:E_2)_\eta\le I(A_1:A_2)_\rho$. Step 1.1 gives $I(B_1:B_2)_\omega\ge0$ by [F6], so the displayed difference is nonpositive. Therefore $F(\mathcal N_1\otimes\mathcal N_2)\le F(\mathcal N_1)+F(\mathcal N_2)$. [F1, F2, F3, F6, step 1.1, algebra]
required_hypotheses_and_conventions: All marginals and joint states use finite ordered tensor factors and the declared partial-trace/reordering convention.
Mutual information and conditional MI are finite entropy expressions; the definition does not itself assert nonnegativity.

claim.text:
Let $\mathcal E_{d,\epsilon}$ be the finite-dimensional erasure channel with data dimension $d\ge1$ and erasure probability $\epsilon\in[0,1]$, with the complementary dilation in [[lem-it-qudit-erasure-channel-complement-and-degradability]]. For every input state $\rho$,

$$I_c(\rho,\mathcal E_{d,\epsilon})=(1-2\epsilon)S(\rho).$$

export.text:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root convention that its inner product is linear in the first argument, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$ ([[def-qc-density-operator]]). If $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$ are its eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, define its **von Neumann entropy** by

$$S(\rho):=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho):=-\sum_{j:\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j\ln\lambda_j.$$

The trace is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]), and the spectral definition makes the expression independent of the eigenbasis. The term for a zero eigenvalue is defined to be $0\ln0:=0$. The default unit is nats, using the natural logarithm ([[def-natural-logarithm]]); the entropy in bits is $S_2(\rho):=S(\rho)/\ln2$.

consumer_proof_or_symbol_use_quotes: 1.1 Apply [F3] to the two states in [F1]. Their entropies are $h(\epsilon)+(1-\epsilon)S(\rho)$ and $h(1-\epsilon)+\epsilon S(\rho)$, respectively. Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root convention that its inner product is linear in the first argument, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$ ([[def-qc-density-operator]]). If $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$ are its eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, define its **von Neumann entropy** by

$$S(\rho):=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho):=-\sum_{j:\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j\ln\lambda_j.$$

The trace is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]), and the spectral definition makes the expression independent of the eigenbasis. The term for a zero eigenvalue is defined to be $0\ln0:=0$. The default unit is nats, using the natural logarithm ([[def-natural-logarithm]]); the entropy in bits is $S_2(\rho):=S(\rho)/\ln2$.

claim.text:
Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional quantum channel and use its memoryless extension $\mathcal N^{\otimes n}:A^{\otimes n}\to B^{\otimes n}$. Rates use natural logarithms, so they are in nats per channel use. For code sizes $K_n\ge1$, a rate $R\ge0$ is achievable when $\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}\ln K_n\ge R$ and the relevant error terms below tend to zero; each capacity is the supremum of its achievable rates.

For **quantum transmission**, a block code consists of an isometric encoder $W_n:M_n\to A^{\otimes n}$ and a quantum-channel decoder $\mathcal D_n:B^{\otimes n}\to M_n$, where $\dim M_n=K_n$. Let $R_n\cong M_n$ and let $|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle\in R_n\otimes M_n$ be a normalized maximally entangled vector. Its entanglement fidelity is

$$F_n:=\langle\Phi_{K_n}|(\operatorname{id}_{R_n}\otimes\mathcal D_n\mathcal N^{\otimes n}\mathcal W_n)(|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle\langle\Phi_{K_n}|)|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle,$$

where $\mathcal W_n(X)=W_nXW_n^*$. A rate is quantum-achievable if $F_n\to1$; the resulting capacity is $Q(\mathcal N)$. This is the subspace entanglement-transmission convention.

For **private classical transmission**, a block code uses equiprobable messages $m\in[K_n]$, input states $\rho_{m,n}$ on $A^{\otimes n}$, and a decoding POVM $\{\Lambda_{m,n}\}_{m=1}^{K_n}$ on $B^{\otimes n}$. Its average error is

$$e_n:=1-\frac1{K_n}\sum_{m=1}^{K_n}\operatorname{tr}(\Lambda_{m,n}\mathcal N^{\otimes n}(\rho_{m,n})).$$

Fix a complementary channel $\mathcal N^c$ as in [[def-it-quantum-channel-complement-and-coherent-information]]. Eve's average state is $\bar\tau_n=K_n^{-1}\sum_m(\mathcal N^c)^{\otimes n}(\rho_{m,n})$. Define leakage by its Holevo information

$$\ell_n:=S(\bar\tau_n)-\frac1{K_n}\sum_{m=1}^{K_n}S((\mathcal N^c)^{\otimes n}(\rho_{m,n})).$$

A rate is privately achievable when $e_n\to0$ and $\ell_n\to0$; this is strong secrecy in mutual-information form. The corresponding capacity is $P(\mathcal N)$. The value is independent of the chosen complementary dilation, as follows from [[lem-it-private-information-is-coherent-information-difference]].

For **classical transmission with prior shared entanglement**, for each block length $n$ the sender and receiver begin with a finite-dimensional shared state $\sigma_{S_AS_B}$ independent of the equiprobable message. For each $m\in[K_n]$, the sender applies a quantum channel $\mathcal E_{m,n}:\mathcal L(S_A)\to\mathcal L(A^{\otimes n})$. The receiver measures $B^{\otimes n}\otimes S_B$ with a POVM $\{\Gamma_{m,n}\}_{m=1}^{K_n}$. Its average error is

$$e_n^{EA}:=1-\frac1{K_n}\sum_{m=1}^{K_n}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[\Gamma_{m,n}\bigl((\mathcal N^{\otimes n}\circ\mathcal E_{m,n})\otimes\operatorname{id}_{S_B}\bigr)(\sigma_{S_AS_B})\right].$$ A rate is achievable when this error tends to zero; there is no constraint on the dimension or consumption of the shared entanglement. The resulting capacity is $C_E(\mathcal N)$.

The input, output, and reference registers are finite-dimensional in each block. No single-letter formula is included in these operational definitions.

export.text:
Let $X$ be a finite nonempty classical label set, represented by a register $H_X$ with computational orthonormal basis $(\xi_x)_{x\in X}$ ([[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]]). For each $x$, write $\Pi_xz:=\langle z,\xi_x\rangle\xi_x$, the rank-one orthogonal projection using the root linear-first convention, as in [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Let $H_B$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. A finite **classical-quantum state** is

$$\rho_{XB}:=\sum_{x\in X}p_x\Pi_x\otimes\rho_x,$$

where $p_x\ge0$, $\sum_xp_x=1$, and each $\rho_x$ is a density operator on $H_B$. It is a density operator by [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Its quantum marginal is $\bar\rho_B:=\sum_xp_x\rho_x=\operatorname{Tr}_X\rho_{XB}$ by the second-factor partial-trace formula in [[def-qc-partial-trace]], and it is a density operator by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. The **Holevo information** of this ensemble is

$$\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\}_{x\in X}):=S(\bar\rho_B)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x),$$

where zero-probability branches contribute nothing. This is measured in nats under [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]].

claim.text:
Let $\mathcal N_i:A_i\to B_i$ for $i=1,2$ be finite-dimensional degradable channels with complements $\mathcal N_i^c=\mathcal D_i\circ\mathcal N_i$. Then $\rho\mapsto I_c(\rho,\mathcal N_i)$ is concave and nonnegative. For every joint input state $\rho_{A_1A_2}$,

$$I_c(\rho_{A_1A_2},\mathcal N_1\otimes\mathcal N_2)\le I_c(\rho_{A_1},\mathcal N_1)+I_c(\rho_{A_2},\mathcal N_2).$$

Consequently the supremum coherent information of $\mathcal N_1\otimes\mathcal N_2$ is the sum of the two single-channel suprema.

Let $H_B$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. A finite **classical-quantum state** is

$$\rho_{XB}:=\sum_{x\in X}p_x\Pi_x\otimes\rho_x,$$

where $p_x\ge0$, $\sum_xp_x=1$, and each $\rho_x$ is a density operator on $H_B$. It is a density operator by [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Its quantum marginal is $\bar\rho_B:=\sum_xp_x\rho_x=\operatorname{Tr}_X\rho_{XB}$ by the second-factor partial-trace formula in [[def-qc-partial-trace]], and it is a density operator by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. The **Holevo information** of this ensemble is

$$\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\}_{x\in X}):=S(\bar\rho_B)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x),$$

where zero-probability branches contribute nothing. This is measured in nats under [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]].

claim.text:
Let $\mathcal N_i:A_i\to B_i$ for $i=1,2$ be finite-dimensional degradable channels with complements $\mathcal N_i^c=\mathcal D_i\circ\mathcal N_i$. Then $\rho\mapsto I_c(\rho,\mathcal N_i)$ is concave and nonnegative. For every joint input state $\rho_{A_1A_2}$,

$$I_c(\rho_{A_1A_2},\mathcal N_1\otimes\mathcal N_2)\le I_c(\rho_{A_1},\mathcal N_1)+I_c(\rho_{A_2},\mathcal N_2).$$

Consequently the supremum coherent information of $\mathcal N_1\otimes\mathcal N_2$ is the sum of the two single-channel suprema.

export.text:
For a finite bipartite state $\rho_{AB}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B$, write $\rho_A=\operatorname{Tr}_B\rho_{AB}$ and $\rho_B=\operatorname{Tr}_A\rho_{AB}$, using the partial traces in [[def-qc-partial-trace]] and [[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]. They are states by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. Define

$$S(A)_\rho:=S(\rho_A),\qquad S(A\mid B)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AB})-S(\rho_B),\qquad I(A:B)_\rho:=S(\rho_A)+S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{AB}).$$

For a finite tripartite state $\rho_{ABC}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C$, set $\rho_{AB}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_C}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying the factors as $(H_A\otimes H_B)\otimes H_C$, and $\rho_{BC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_A}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying them as $H_A\otimes(H_B\otimes H_C)$. Let $P:H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C\to H_A\otimes H_C\otimes H_B$ be the wire permutation taking factor order $A,B,C$ to $A,C,B$ ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]) and set $\rho_{AC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}(P\rho_{ABC}P^*)$, tracing out the last factor. Because $P$ is unitary, $P\rho_{ABC}P^*$ is a state: unitary conjugation preserves non-negativity by the adjoint identity ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]) and preserves trace by cyclicity ([[thm-trace-of-ab-equals-trace-of-ba]]). Finally set $\rho_C:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}\rho_{BC}$. All these marginals are density operators by applying [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]] after grouping factors. Define

$$I(A:B\mid C)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AC})+S(\rho_{BC})-S(\rho_C)-S(\rho_{ABC}).$$

These are finite-dimensional definitions only; no non-negativity of conditional entropy or conditional mutual information is part of the notation.

export.text:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root convention that its inner product is linear in the first argument, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$ ([[def-qc-density-operator]]). If $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$ are its eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, define its **von Neumann entropy** by

$$S(\rho):=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho):=-\sum_{j:\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j\ln\lambda_j.$$

The trace is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]), and the spectral definition makes the expression independent of the eigenbasis. The term for a zero eigenvalue is defined to be $0\ln0:=0$. The default unit is nats, using the natural logarithm ([[def-natural-logarithm]]); the entropy in bits is $S_2(\rho):=S(\rho)/\ln2$.

export.text:
Let $x\mapsto\rho_x$ be a finite-input, finite-output memoryless cq channel as in [[def-it-classical-quantum-memoryless-channel]]. With the average-error code convention of [[def-it-cq-channel-block-code-and-error]], its classical capacity in nats per use is
$$C_{\rm cq}=\max_{p\in\Delta(\mathcal X)}\chi_p,\qquad \chi_p:=S\!\left(\sum_xp_x\rho_x\right)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x).$$
For every $0\le R<C_{\rm cq}$ a sequence of codes with rate tending to $R$ has average error tending to zero, and every reliable sequence has limiting upper rate at most $C_{\rm cq}$. This theorem concerns a fixed finite classical input alphabet and does not assert a single-letter formula for general quantum-input channels.

Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional memoryless quantum channel. For each $n\ge1$, let

$$p_n(\mathcal N):=\sup_{\mathcal E_n} I_p(\mathcal E_n,\mathcal N^{\otimes n}),$$

where the supremum ranges over all finite ensembles of input states on $A^{\otimes n}$. Under the strong-secrecy, average-error convention in [[def-it-quantum-channel-operational-capacities]],

$$P(\mathcal N)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{p_n(\mathcal N)}n=\sup_{n\ge1}\frac{p_n(\mathcal N)}n.$$

This statement is regularized and asserts no general single-letter formula.

export.text:
For a finite bipartite state $\rho_{AB}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B$, write $\rho_A=\operatorname{Tr}_B\rho_{AB}$ and $\rho_B=\operatorname{Tr}_A\rho_{AB}$, using the partial traces in [[def-qc-partial-trace]] and [[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]. They are states by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. Define

$$S(A)_\rho:=S(\rho_A),\qquad S(A\mid B)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AB})-S(\rho_B),\qquad I(A:B)_\rho:=S(\rho_A)+S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{AB}).$$

For a finite tripartite state $\rho_{ABC}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C$, set $\rho_{AB}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_C}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying the factors as $(H_A\otimes H_B)\otimes H_C$, and $\rho_{BC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_A}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying them as $H_A\otimes(H_B\otimes H_C)$. Let $P:H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C\to H_A\otimes H_C\otimes H_B$ be the wire permutation taking factor order $A,B,C$ to $A,C,B$ ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]) and set $\rho_{AC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}(P\rho_{ABC}P^*)$, tracing out the last factor. Because $P$ is unitary, $P\rho_{ABC}P^*$ is a state: unitary conjugation preserves non-negativity by the adjoint identity ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]) and preserves trace by cyclicity ([[thm-trace-of-ab-equals-trace-of-ba]]). Finally set $\rho_C:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}\rho_{BC}$. All these marginals are density operators by applying [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]] after grouping factors. Define

$$I(A:B\mid C)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AC})+S(\rho_{BC})-S(\rho_C)-S(\rho_{ABC}).$$

These are finite-dimensional definitions only; no non-negativity of conditional entropy or conditional mutual information is part of the notation.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root convention that its inner product is linear in the first argument, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$ ([[def-qc-density-operator]]). If $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$ are its eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, define its **von Neumann entropy** by

$$S(\rho):=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho):=-\sum_{j:\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j\ln\lambda_j.$$

The trace is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]), and the spectral definition makes the expression independent of the eigenbasis. The term for a zero eigenvalue is defined to be $0\ln0:=0$. The default unit is nats, using the natural logarithm ([[def-natural-logarithm]]); the entropy in bits is $S_2(\rho):=S(\rho)/\ln2$.

Let $X$ be a finite nonempty classical label set, represented by a register $H_X$ with computational orthonormal basis $(\xi_x)_{x\in X}$ ([[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]]). For each $x$, write $\Pi_xz:=\langle z,\xi_x\rangle\xi_x$, the rank-one orthogonal projection using the root linear-first convention, as in [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Let $H_B$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. A finite **classical-quantum state** is

$$\rho_{XB}:=\sum_{x\in X}p_x\Pi_x\otimes\rho_x,$$

where $p_x\ge0$, $\sum_xp_x=1$, and each $\rho_x$ is a density operator on $H_B$. It is a density operator by [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Its quantum marginal is $\bar\rho_B:=\sum_xp_x\rho_x=\operatorname{Tr}_X\rho_{XB}$ by the second-factor partial-trace formula in [[def-qc-partial-trace]], and it is a density operator by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. The **Holevo information** of this ensemble is

$$\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\}_{x\in X}):=S(\bar\rho_B)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x),$$

where zero-probability branches contribute nothing. This is measured in nats under [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]].

export.text:
Let $X$ take values in an alphabet $\mathcal X$ of size $m\ge2$, let $Y$ be finite, and let $\widehat X$ be an estimator in the same alphabet generated from $Y$, so the joint pmf factors as $p_{XY\widehat X}=p_{XY}p_{\widehat X|Y}$. Put $P_e=\mathbb P[\widehat X\ne X]$ and define

$$h_2(t):=-t\ln t-(1-t)\ln(1-t),\qquad 0\ln0:=0.$$

Then

$$H(X|Y)\le h_2(P_e)+P_e\ln(m-1)\le \ln2+P_e\ln m.$$

For $m=1$, $X$ is constant and $H(X|Y)=0$.

consumer_proof_or_symbol_use_quotes: 3.1 Apply the construction to any finite ensemble of inputs for a fixed block channel $\mathcal N^{\otimes j}$. Each code uses a finite average of tensor products of those possibly mixed block inputs, permitted by the operational model. Group its blocks and pad fewer than $j$ leftover original-channel uses with a fixed state. The extra complementary state is independent of the message, so leakage is unchanged by tensoring it; the decoder discards the extra receiver output. Hence $P(\mathcal N)\ge p_j/j$ for every $j$: approximate the finite-ensemble supremum first, then take an arbitrary rate strictly below its private information. The stated Fekete argument gives the entire regularized direct bound. [F9, F10, F11, step 2.1, given, algebra, construct]

4.1 For any uniform $M$-message code, let $\widehat M$ be Bob's decoded message and $e$ its average error. Write $h(u)=-u\ln u-(1-u)\ln(1-u)$, with continuous endpoint values. The finite Fano inequality gives $H(M\mid\widehat M)\le h(e)+e\ln(M-1)\le h(e)+e\ln M$ for $M\ge2$. The Holevo measurement bound, applied to the finite receiver ensemble, gives $I(M;\widehat M)\le\chi_B$. Therefore $$(1-e)\ln M\le\chi_B+h(e).$$ The uniform input ensemble $\{M^{-1},\rho_{m,n}\}$ is among those defining $p_n$, and its private information is $\chi_B-\ell_n$. Thus $$(1-e)\ln M\le p_n+\ell_n+h(e).$$ For $M=1$, the desired asymptotic bound is trivial. For a reliable strongly secret sequence, divide by $n$; since $p_n/n$ is bounded and $e_n\to0$, the displayed inequality itself bounds $\ln M_n/n$, even though no dimension-based bound on the number of repeated classical messages was assumed. The terms $\ell_n/n$ and $h(e_n)/n$ vanish. This proves the converse for the stated liminf-achievable rate convention and the retained full equality $P=\lim_n p_n/n=\sup_n p_n/n$. [F9, F10, F11, step 3.1, given, algebra, construct] ∎

export.text:
For a finite bipartite state $\rho_{AB}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B$, write $\rho_A=\operatorname{Tr}_B\rho_{AB}$ and $\rho_B=\operatorname{Tr}_A\rho_{AB}$, using the partial traces in [[def-qc-partial-trace]] and [[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]. They are states by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. Define

$$S(A)_\rho:=S(\rho_A),\qquad S(A\mid B)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AB})-S(\rho_B),\qquad I(A:B)_\rho:=S(\rho_A)+S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{AB}).$$

For a finite tripartite state $\rho_{ABC}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C$, set $\rho_{AB}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_C}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying the factors as $(H_A\otimes H_B)\otimes H_C$, and $\rho_{BC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_A}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying them as $H_A\otimes(H_B\otimes H_C)$. Let $P:H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C\to H_A\otimes H_C\otimes H_B$ be the wire permutation taking factor order $A,B,C$ to $A,C,B$ ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]) and set $\rho_{AC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}(P\rho_{ABC}P^*)$, tracing out the last factor. Because $P$ is unitary, $P\rho_{ABC}P^*$ is a state: unitary conjugation preserves non-negativity by the adjoint identity ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]) and preserves trace by cyclicity ([[thm-trace-of-ab-equals-trace-of-ba]]). Finally set $\rho_C:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}\rho_{BC}$. All these marginals are density operators by applying [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]] after grouping factors. Define

$$I(A:B\mid C)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AC})+S(\rho_{BC})-S(\rho_C)-S(\rho_{ABC}).$$

These are finite-dimensional definitions only; no non-negativity of conditional entropy or conditional mutual information is part of the notation.

export.text:
Let $\rho$ be a density operator on a nonzero finite-dimensional source space, and use the squared entanglement-fidelity code model of [[def-it-quantum-source-and-compression-code]]. Write $S(\rho)$ in nats.

1. For every $R>S(\rho)$ there is a sequence of compression codes with $F_e^{(n)}\to1$ and $\limsup_n n^{-1}\ln M_n\le R$.
2. If a sequence of codes satisfies $\limsup_n n^{-1}\ln M_n<S(\rho)$, then $F_e^{(n)}\to0$.

Thus the asymptotic reliable compression rate is exactly $S(\rho)$ nats per source letter, or $S(\rho)/\ln2$ qubits per source letter.

Let $x\mapsto\rho_x$ be a finite-input, finite-output memoryless cq channel as in [[def-it-classical-quantum-memoryless-channel]]. With the average-error code convention of [[def-it-cq-channel-block-code-and-error]], its classical capacity in nats per use is

For every $0\le R<C_{\rm cq}$ a sequence of codes with rate tending to $R$ has average error tending to zero, and every reliable sequence has limiting upper rate at most $C_{\rm cq}$. export.text:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root convention that its inner product is linear in the first argument, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$ ([[def-qc-density-operator]]). If $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$ are its eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, define its **von Neumann entropy** by

$$S(\rho):=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho):=-\sum_{j:\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j\ln\lambda_j.$$

The trace is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]), and the spectral definition makes the expression independent of the eigenbasis. The term for a zero eigenvalue is defined to be $0\ln0:=0$. The default unit is nats, using the natural logarithm ([[def-natural-logarithm]]); the entropy in bits is $S_2(\rho):=S(\rho)/\ln2$.

previous_native_observation.excerpt:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root convention that its inner product is linear in the first argument, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$ ([[def-qc-density-operator]]). If $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$ are its eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, define its **von Neumann entropy** by

$$S(\rho):=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho):=-\sum_{j:\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j\ln\lambda_j.$$

The trace is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]), and the spectral definition makes the expression independent of the eigenbasis. The term for a zero eigenvalue is defined to be $0\ln0:=0$. The default unit is nats, using the natural logarithm ([[def-natural-logarithm]]); the entropy in bits is $S_2(\rho):=S(\rho)/\ln2$.

claim.text:
Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional quantum channel. Under the shared-entanglement coding convention in [[def-it-quantum-channel-operational-capacities]],

$$C_E(\mathcal N)=\max_{\rho\in\mathcal D(A)}\bigl(S(\rho)+I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)\bigr)=\max_{\rho\in\mathcal D(A)}I(R;B)_{(\operatorname{id}_R\otimes\mathcal N)(\psi_\rho)},$$

where $\psi_\rho$ is any finite purification of $\rho$ on $R\otimes A$. The value is additive: $C_E(\mathcal N_1\otimes\mathcal N_2)=C_E(\mathcal N_1)+C_E(\mathcal N_2)$ for finite-dimensional channels.

export.text:
Let $X$ take values in an alphabet $\mathcal X$ of size $m\ge2$, let $Y$ be finite, and let $\widehat X$ be an estimator in the same alphabet generated from $Y$, so the joint pmf factors as $p_{XY\widehat X}=p_{XY}p_{\widehat X|Y}$. Put $P_e=\mathbb P[\widehat X\ne X]$ and define

$$h_2(t):=-t\ln t-(1-t)\ln(1-t),\qquad 0\ln0:=0.$$

Then

$$H(X|Y)\le h_2(P_e)+P_e\ln(m-1)\le \ln2+P_e\ln m.$$

For $m=1$, $X$ is constant and $H(X|Y)=0$.

consumer_proof_or_symbol_use_quotes: 2.1 For any input state $\rho$ and positive integer $m$, exact spectral type reduction gives a flat state $\tau_t$ on an $m$-use input subspace such that $$f_{\mathcal N^{\otimes m}}(\tau_t)\ge m f_{\mathcal N}(\rho)-2d\ln(m+1),\qquad d=\dim A.$$ Apply the flat-state construction to that fixed block channel. For fixed $m$, both its Weyl alphabet and its receiver output dimension are finite, so the HSW theorem applies before any limit in $m$ is taken. The shared resource is the flat type-subspace maximally entangled state for each outer block. Padding fewer than $m$ unused original-channel inputs with a fixed state gives codes for all sufficiently large lengths and no asymptotic rate loss. Therefore $$C_E(\mathcal N)\ge f_{\mathcal N}(\rho)-\frac{2d\ln(m+1)}m.$$ Let $m\to\infty$ and maximize over $\rho$. This proves the general direct bound with precisely the stated unlimited finite-shared-entanglement model. No unrestricted quantum-input HSW single-letter theorem and no inference from Schumacher compression alone is used. [F5, F6, F7, F8, F9, F10, step 1.2, given, algebra, construct]

3.1 Consider any length-$n$ stated EA code with uniform message register $M$, receiver's prior share $S$, channel input $A^n$, and receiver output $B^nS$. Before transmission its joint state is $$\omega_{MA^nS}=\frac1K\sum_m|m\rangle\langle m|\otimes(\mathcal E_m\otimes\operatorname{id}_S)(\sigma).$$ The marginal $MS$ is the product of the uniform message and the original share: each encoder is trace-preserving and hence cannot change $S$. In particular $I(M:S)=0$. Let $\bar\rho_{A^n}$ be its average input. By the extension lemma, the $MSA^n$ state is obtained by a channel on the reference of a purification of $\bar\rho_{A^n}$. After transmission, quantum-mutual-information data processing gives $$I(MS:B^n)\le I(R:B^n)_{(\operatorname{id}\otimes\mathcal N^{\otimes n})(\psi_{\bar\rho})}.$$ Expanding the entropy definitions gives the exact identity $$I(M:B^nS)=I(MS:B^n)-I(S:B^n)+I(M:S).$$ The last term is zero, and $I(S:B^n)\ge0$ by subadditivity. Therefore $$I(M:B^nS)\le I(R:B^n)\le F(\mathcal N^{\otimes n})=nF(\mathcal N).$$ The equality uses the stated optimized-information additivity lemma, whose proof follows local-channel mutual-information data processing and product-state entropy additivity. Write $h(u)=-u\ln u-(1-u)\ln(1-u)$ with continuous endpoint values. Bob's POVM and the Holevo bound imply $I(M;\widehat M)\le I(M:B^nS)$. Fano then gives $$(1-e_n)\ln K_n\le nF(\mathcal N)+h(e_n).$$ Singleton message sets are trivial. Divide by $n$ and let average error tend to zero to bound every achievable rate by $F(\mathcal N)$, without restricting the shared state, its dimension, or the message-dependent CPTP encoders. Together with the general direct bound, purification identity and attained maximum, this proves the entire retained operational formula. Finally applying the identity $C_E=F$ to both channels and their product, and using the stated proved additivity of $F$, proves the capacity additivity assertion as well. [F5, F6, F7, F8, F9, F10, step 2.1, given, algebra, construct] ∎

export.text:
Let $X$ be a finite nonempty set, let $(p_x)$ be a probability vector, let $\rho_x$ be density operators on a nonzero finite-dimensional space $H_B$, and let $\bar\rho:=\sum_xp_x\rho_x$. For a finite POVM $(E_y)_{y\in Y}$ on $H_B$, define $w(y\mid x):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_xE_y)$, $q_y:=\sum_xp_xw(y\mid x)$, and the classical mutual information

$$I(X:Y):=\sum_{x,y:p_xw(y\mid x)>0}p_xw(y\mid x)\ln\frac{w(y\mid x)}{q_y}.$$

Then

$$I(X:Y)\le\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\})=S(\bar\rho)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x).$$

claim.text:
For the finite-dimensional flagged erasure channel $\mathcal E_{d,\epsilon}$ with input dimension $d\ge1$ and erasure probability $\epsilon\in[0,1]$,

$$Q(\mathcal E_{d,\epsilon})=P(\mathcal E_{d,\epsilon})=\max\{1-2\epsilon,0\}\ln d,\qquad C_E(\mathcal E_{d,\epsilon})=2(1-\epsilon)\ln d.$$

All capacities are in nats per channel use. The unassisted quantum and private formulas are zero in the antidegradable regime $\epsilon\ge1/2$.

export.text:
For a finite bipartite state $\rho_{AB}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B$, write $\rho_A=\operatorname{Tr}_B\rho_{AB}$ and $\rho_B=\operatorname{Tr}_A\rho_{AB}$, using the partial traces in [[def-qc-partial-trace]] and [[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]. They are states by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. Define

$$S(A)_\rho:=S(\rho_A),\qquad S(A\mid B)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AB})-S(\rho_B),\qquad I(A:B)_\rho:=S(\rho_A)+S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{AB}).$$

For a finite tripartite state $\rho_{ABC}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C$, set $\rho_{AB}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_C}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying the factors as $(H_A\otimes H_B)\otimes H_C$, and $\rho_{BC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_A}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying them as $H_A\otimes(H_B\otimes H_C)$. Let $P:H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C\to H_A\otimes H_C\otimes H_B$ be the wire permutation taking factor order $A,B,C$ to $A,C,B$ ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]) and set $\rho_{AC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}(P\rho_{ABC}P^*)$, tracing out the last factor. Because $P$ is unitary, $P\rho_{ABC}P^*$ is a state: unitary conjugation preserves non-negativity by the adjoint identity ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]) and preserves trace by cyclicity ([[thm-trace-of-ab-equals-trace-of-ba]]). Finally set $\rho_C:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}\rho_{BC}$. All these marginals are density operators by applying [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]] after grouping factors. Define

$$I(A:B\mid C)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AC})+S(\rho_{BC})-S(\rho_C)-S(\rho_{ABC}).$$

These are finite-dimensional definitions only; no non-negativity of conditional entropy or conditional mutual information is part of the notation.

consumer_proof_or_symbol_use_quotes: 1.2 Now suppose $\epsilon\ge1/2$. By [F2], there is an antidegrading channel $\mathcal A:E\to B$ with $\mathcal E=\mathcal A\circ\mathcal E^c$. Its tensor powers are channels by [F9]. For any $n$-use input state and purification reference $R$, [F5] gives $I(R;B^n)\le I(R;E^n)$. The joint state $RB^nE^n$ from a product Stinespring isometry is pure, so its $B^n$ and $RE^n$ marginals have equal entropy and its $E^n$ and $RB^n$ marginals have equal entropy by Schmidt decomposition. Thus $I_c(\rho,\mathcal E^{\otimes n})=S(B^n)-S(E^n)\le0$. A pure input attains zero, so the $n$-use coherent-information supremum is zero and [F4] gives $Q=0$. [F2, F4, F5, F6, F9, F10, given, algebra]

2.2 For any finite $n$-use ensemble, [F7] and [F6] express private information as $I(X;B^n)-I(X;E^n)$. The antidegrading channel on $E^n$ and [F5] make this difference nonpositive. The singleton ensemble has private information zero, so each $n$-use private-information supremum is zero; [F4] gives $P=0$. [F4, F5, F6, F7, step 1.2, algebra]

For a finite-dimensional bipartite state $\rho_{AB}$,

$$I(A:B)_\rho=S(\rho_A)+S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{AB})=D(\rho_{AB}\|\rho_A\otimes\rho_B).$$

For a finite classical-quantum state $\rho_{XB}=\sum_xp_x\Pi_x\otimes\rho_x$, its mutual information equals its Holevo information:

$$I(X:B)_\rho=S\!\left(\sum_xp_x\rho_x\right)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x)=\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\}).$$

Thus $I_c(\rho,\mathcal E^{\otimes n})=S(B^n)-S(E^n)\le0$. A pure input attains zero, so the $n$-use coherent-information supremum is zero and [F4] gives $Q=0$. export.text:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root convention that its inner product is linear in the first argument, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$ ([[def-qc-density-operator]]). If $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$ are its eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, define its **von Neumann entropy** by

$$S(\rho):=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho):=-\sum_{j:\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j\ln\lambda_j.$$

The trace is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]), and the spectral definition makes the expression independent of the eigenbasis. The term for a zero eigenvalue is defined to be $0\ln0:=0$. The default unit is nats, using the natural logarithm ([[def-natural-logarithm]]); the entropy in bits is $S_2(\rho):=S(\rho)/\ln2$.

export.text:
Write $\ln$ for the natural logarithm $\log$ of [[def-natural-logarithm]]. Unless a base is displayed, every information quantity on this page uses $\ln$ and is measured in **nats**. For a base $b>1$ and $t>0$, define
$$\log_b t:=\frac{\ln t}{\ln b}.$$
The denominator is positive: $b>1$, $\ln$ is strictly increasing, and $\ln 1=0$ by [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]. A base-$b$ entropy or divergence is obtained by replacing each $\ln$ in the finite formulas below by $\log_b$; use $0\log_b0:=0$ and assign $+\infty$ to a positive numerator over a zero denominator. The case $b=2$ measures **bits**; $b=e$ gives nats.
